name: Shattering Formula and Sharp Costs for Conjunction Substitution
statement: Let $A=C[i=0]$, $B=C[i=1]$, replace $i$ by conjunction on $k\ge2$ fresh coordinates $Z$, and call the result $D$. For $S\subseteq X,T\subseteq Z$, $S\sqcup T$ is shattered by $D$ exactly when: $S\in\operatorname{Sh}(A\cup B)$ for $T=\varnothing$; $S\in\operatorname{Sh}(A)$ for $0<|T|<k$; and $S\sqcup\{i\}\in\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ for $T=Z$. If $C$ is maximum of rank $r\ge1$, then $\operatorname{VC}(D)=h(D)=r+k-1$. For $r\le n-2$, every parent uses at least $k-1$ auxiliaries and the bound is attained. If $r=n$, the exact count is zero. If $r=n-1$ and $C=Q^n\setminus\{v\}$, it is zero for $v_i=1$ and $k-1$ for $v_i=0$.
proof: Empty, proper, and full subsets of the conjunction coordinates respectively see the old projection, force old value zero, or distinguish both old values, yielding the three shattering cases. A full reduction supplies an $(r-1)$-cube times the new cube, attaining VC dimension $r+k-1$, while iterated conjunction gives a parent at that rank with $k-1$ auxiliaries. A minimally missing old pattern lifts to support $R+1$ in any rank-$R$ parent and forces the matching auxiliary lower bound; direct inspection handles the two top-rank boundaries.
